Generate Color Palettes

Source: R/15-color-palette.R
color_palette.Rd

`color_palette()` returns curated palettes for data visualization. It supports both the legacy numeric interface and a newer named interface for journal- and media-inspired palettes.

Usage

color_palette(palette = NULL, palette_number = NULL, show_all = FALSE)

Arguments

palette

Character. Name of the palette to return. Supported values are `"nature"`, `"science"`, `"cell"`, `"economist"`, `"bbc"`, `"nytimes"`, and `"legacy5"`.

palette_number

Integer. Legacy interface. Currently only `5` is supported and returns the original list of five-color palettes.

show_all

Logical. If `TRUE`, return all available palettes as a named list.

Value

If `palette` is provided, a character vector of hex colors.

If `show_all = TRUE`, a named list of all palettes.

If `palette_number = 5`, the original list of five-color palettes.

Details

The named palettes are intended for practical plotting rather than strict brand replication.

  • `"nature"` is based on the well-known Nature Publishing Group style palette commonly used in scientific figures.

  • `"science"` is based on the widely used AAAS/Science style palette.

  • `"cell"`, `"economist"`, `"bbc"`, and `"nytimes"` are editorial or publication-inspired palettes curated for clear categorical contrast.

  • `palette_number = 5` preserves the original package behavior.

Examples

# New named interface
color_palette("nature")
#> [1] "#E64B35" "#4DBBD5" "#00A087" "#3C5488" "#F39B7F" "#8491B4"
color_palette("economist")
#> [1] "#E3120B" "#006BA2" "#3EBCD2" "#379A8B" "#EAC435" "#8E6C8A"

# Return all named palettes
names(color_palette(show_all = TRUE))
#> [1] "nature"    "science"   "cell"      "economist" "bbc"       "nytimes"  
#> [7] "legacy5"  

# Legacy interface
legacy_palettes <- color_palette(palette_number = 5)
legacy_palettes[[1]]
#> [1] "#2C3E50" "#E74C3C" "#ECF0F1" "#3498DB" "#2980B9"
